correctness.rationale: Headline is a CONDITIONAL envelope-closure arithmetic fact, honestly scoped as obstruction to the admitted route, not a distance-measure theorem. Verified: (a) Definitions match Raani-Singh fetched primary: H^1=CxR with (z,t).(w,s)=(z+w,t+s+1/2 Im(z\bar w)), Koranyi norm (|z|^4+t^2)^{1/4}, Q=4, mu=2(2k+1) at n=1, Lemma 1.4 exponent n/2-1/4=1/4. (b) Conditional lemma math re-derived independently: M(t)=int_0^{R0} r^6 min(1,(t r^2)^-1/2)dr with rs=t^-1/2 gives M=R0^7/7 for t<=R0^-2 else rs^7/7+t^-1/2(R0^6-rs^6)/6 =R0^6/6 t^-1/2 -t^-7/2/42; large-t ratio ~const t^{alpha-1/2} so bounded iff alpha<=1/2 for the feasible dimension range alpha=4-s' in [0,4]. Replayed threshold_closure.py exactly (alpha 0.5 sup 10.6667 bounded; alpha 1.0 sup 106666.7 growing ~t^1/2) and Simpson cross-check; replayed check_Rk_decay.py exactly (R(0)=1, worst |R|/rho^-1/4=0.970). (c) Proof vs evidence distinguished: envelope (E) is cited from Raani-Singh Lemma 1.4, only numerically consistency-checked, explicitly not re-proved; closure iff is proved analytically; no positive-measure theorem at 3 or 7/2 claimed. Minor exposition slip: proof sentence 't^-alpha->inf as t->0' holds only for alpha>0; for feasible s' in [0,4] (alpha in [0,4]) the iff conclusion remains true (alpha=0 gives bounded M). Out-of-domain alpha<0 (s'>Q, impossible for subsets of H^1) would diverge at 0 but is irrelevant to headline cases alpha=0.5/1.0. Weight r^6 and squared-envelope reduction are part of the admitted route definition; fuller Frostman trace/uniformity gaps explicitly deferred as limitations, so no overclaim.
